items.description: A link description object is used to describe link relations.  In the context of a schema, it defines the link relations of the instances of the schema, and can be parameterized by the instance values.  The link description format can be used on its own in regular (non-schema) documents, and use of this format can be declared by referencing the normative link description schema as the schema for the data structure that uses the links.

linkID.description: Simple (string) identifier of an object to be used when there is no appropriate specific named ID Type

href.description: The URI of the related entity, typically used to represent any internet or social network address

rel.description: Indicates the nature of the relationship of the related resource to the resource that generated this representation

canonicalUri.description: A unique identifier of the feature/function/operation that the link points to

title.description: This property defines a title for the link.  The value must be a string. User agents MAY use this title when presenting the link to the user.

mediaType.description: The media type that the linked resource will return (Response) in

method.description: The HTTP method code (HTTP Verb) traverse the link (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE)

argumentName.description: Argument name to be passed in

argumentPath.description: Argument path, if referenced from within the body

argumentValue.description: Argument name to be passed in

linkTags.description: Collection of tags to indicate additional natures or aspects of the link. User agents MAY use these tags when presenting the link to the user to provide visual cues of the link's purpose

items.description: Basic common representation of a tag

tagValues.description: A list of the tag values

_meta.description: Meta contains the metadata associated with a response.  A GET response may include metadata to support pagination.

startSequence.description: The instance resource sequence (number) identifying the first resource returned in the response. The server generates this sequence.  It is used by the client to determine the start sequence of the subsequent Get request

completeIndicator.description: Indicates whether the response completes the return of all of the resources of the instance resource set to the requesting system

number.description: Number of instance resources in the response

totalNumber.description: Number of total instance resources in an instance resource set. Note: An instance resource set is a set of instance resources that is determined by a server to satisfy the sets membership criteria (i.e., selection, filter, expansion and search criteria) of a resource management operation (e.g. GET request) upon a collection resource

resourceSetID.description: Unique identifier of the instance resource set.  It is generated by the server as a result of the original Get request
